dish: A short, seasonal menu — snacks like deviled eggs, a seasonal soup, a couple of pastas and entrées such as halibut
w: A small Monroe Street dining room in a century-old brick building whose chef-owners Itaru Nagano and Andrew Kroeger won the 2023 James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest — the third Madison chef ever to take it.

dish: Wisconsin-farm small plates that rotate weekly, and a Friday-night fish fry
w: Produce-forward small plates from an open kitchen on East Washington, built on Wisconsin farms and local spirits. Its chefs have been James Beard semifinalists in two separate years — Sean Pharr (2024) and Kasey Lee Cooke (2026) — and Travel Wisconsin puts it in its first-timer's guide to eating in Madison.

dish: The seasonal farm-to-table tasting menu, sourced from 200+ local vendors
w: Madison's founding farm-to-table restaurant (Odessa Piper, 1976) on the Capitol Square — two of its chefs, Piper (2001) and Tory Miller (2012), won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest. Time Out's Madison list calls it out for working with more than 200 local vendors.

dish: Seasonal farm-to-table gastropub plates with a view of the Capitol
w: Tory Miller's more casual, glass-walled sibling to L'Etoile on the Square (opened 2010), still farm-sourced; Madison Magazine marked its 15th year.

dish: The famously massive Scrambler, plate-sized pancakes and crispy hash browns (cash only)
w: A cash-only breakfast diner across from Camp Randall since 1947, with a reader-board menu and portions of legend. First on Time Out's Madison list; the Cap Times covered the founding family handing it to new owners rather than closing it.

dish: Thick hand-made burgers cooked to order, with 14 cheeses to choose from
w: A longstanding campus-edge burger institution off State Street, its ceiling hung with kites and memorabilia. On Time Out's Madison list; Isthmus calls burgers 'the heart and soul of Dotty's'.

dish: Shared Spanish/French/Italian small plates — the gnocchi and the beet salad
n: A Pig in a Fur Coat
w: A small Willy Street room serving rich, constantly changing Mediterranean-European small plates built on local ingredients; reserve ahead. On Time Out's Madison list.

dish: Saturday-morning cheese curds, cheese bread and in-season produce sold by the people who made them
w: America's largest producers-only farmers' market (founded 1972): on summer Saturdays some 150 Wisconsin growers and cheesemakers completely encircle the State Capitol, and everything is grown or made by the person behind the stand. Time Out ranks it among the country's best.
A European-style cut-to-order cheese shop on the Capitol Square since 2007, showcasing award-winning Wisconsin artisan cheesemakers — the obvious place to taste the state's cheese beyond curds.

dish: Laotian classics — moak pa (fish steamed in banana leaf), curry squash, larb and the eggrolls
w: Madison's first Laotian restaurant, family-run since 1989; the original Willy Street room closed in 2022 but the Atwood Avenue location carries on. On Time Out's Madison list and profiled by Brava and Experience Wisconsin.

dish: Bob's Bad Breath Burger — half a pound with cream cheese, green goddess, caramelized onions and garlic
w: A dim, deep-booth Willy Street pub since 2002, walls lined with travel posters; its award-winning burger is the order. On Time Out's Madison list and in the 2025 reader vote for best bar food.

dish: Diner breakfasts and blue-plate specials in a converted Atwood gas station
w: A retro east-side diner in a former gas station on Atwood Avenue; on Time Out's Madison list and the State Journal's ranking of Madison's favourite breakfast spots.

dish: Mac n' cheese pizza by the slice, served until 2:30am
w: The late-night State Street slice shop that made mac-and-cheese pizza a Madison rite of passage. On Time Out's Madison restaurant list and its best-things-to-do roundup.
